rules.statement: a skill whose fact inventory is empty needs no retrieval testing; stop instead of fabricating queries
the harness is required and user-specified; there is no default and it is never assumed or auto-detected

the fact inventory is rebuilt fresh from the current doc every campaign (the manifest is a diff baseline, never a cache); ids are minted by inventory-mint, never assigned by hand; the manifest is never hand-maintained between campaigns
the skill is never synced into the control workspace
planned spend (entries x 2 arms x reps runs) is confirmed by the user before the first eval run, every campaign, including re-runs
the manifest is recorded only after a completed full campaign, never an aborted campaign, never a mini-campaign
failures are fixed by editing the doc, never by adding behavioral rules, prohibitions, or 'always read X first' discipline clauses
doc fixes are applied between campaigns, never mid-campaign; complete the full pass, then apply edits
recommended edits are presented to the user and applied only after confirmation
queries are kept verbatim within and across campaigns, {RUN_DIR} token included; a bad query is pruned and said so, not rewritten
a scenario still failing after a doc fix gets one more doc revision; if it still fails after that, it is surfaced to the user rather than revised again
fact text is deleted from the source SKILL.md only at 3 consecutive control passes and with user confirmation
the per-run prompt is the bare query text; never put rubric text in a run prompt, never provide additional information, never let the eval agent know this is a test
a query never names the section or file holding the fact it tests
score from answer_text only, never what the agent claims it did or found

wrong-track scope guidance (trigger questions belong to trigger-testing); this track never runs other tracks' scenarios
restatement of the doc-fix norm; deduped into R-improving-the-skill-definition-01
process guidance; the concrete no-default norm it carries is inventoried as the harness rule in this section
restatement of the fresh-inventory norm; deduped into the fact-inventory rule
restatement of the apply-edits-after-confirmation norm; deduped into the improving-the-skill-definition rule
fact-classification guidance (retention tests, drop rationales); how-to with no competing incentive

clustering/mining guidance; how-to with no competing incentive
manifest data hygiene (single source, no duplicated query text); weak temptation, no pressure story
ablation/status mechanics (control-only queries when every covering fact carries status); harness behavior, not agent choice

entry id stability and schema field descriptions; data conventions with no compliance cost
